selector.rationale: Medullary breast cancer is supported by the presence of a dense lymphoid infiltrate and the epithelial cells being negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu, which aligns with the characteristics of this disease.

rejected.label: Inflammatory Breast Cancer
rejected.why: Inflammatory Breast Cancer is contradicted by the lack of overlying skin changes and absence of axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, which are typical features of this condition.

rejected.label: Lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma of the breast
rejected.why: Lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma of the breast lacks specific supporting evidence in the vignette.

rejected.label: Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
rejected.why: While Triple-Negative Breast Cancer shares some characteristics with the case, such as negativity for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu, Medullary breast cancer is more specifically supported by the presence of a dense lymphoid infiltrate.
